A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AraLLaMA research. All 16 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including figures, tables, algorithms and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original AraLLaMA benchmark evaluations, tokenizer compression measurements and TinyLLaMA vocabulary-expansion ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds comparative tokenizer measurements and a repeated-trial decoding-speed experiment.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, progressive vocabulary expansion, expansion schedules and ALAN instruction generation are retained. Section 4.2 newly describes averaging constituent-token embeddings for initialization, but does not establish a change from the procedure used in v1.

E1.justification: Training corpora and Arabic/English knowledge, reasoning, cultural-alignment and instruction-following coverage are retained. The benchmark overview moves from v1 Table 1 to v2 Table 7. The added efficiency measurements concern existing Arabic tokenization and generation tasks without establishing a new domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: v1 Section 6.2 compares AraLLaMA tokenization with LLaMA/AceGPT. v2 Table 1 adds Bloomz, Mistral and Jais to that specific comparison. Comparator membership in the downstream benchmark and TinyLLaMA ablation tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 extends tokenizer evaluation to subword fertility, word integrity and Rényi efficiency. Its new decoding experiment tests 7B chat models with standardized Arabic prompts, a 100-token output cap, exclusion of non-Arabic outputs, and token/word throughput metrics. Existing accuracy protocols and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 3.3 and 6.3 add targeted analyses of word fragmentation, vocabulary utilization and whether tokenization efficiency translates into faster word generation. The existing uniform-versus-exponential comparison and progressive-versus-one-shot ablations, including the appendix loss curves, are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Section 6.3 newly reports five independent timing trials, uncertainty values in Table 6 and p > 0.05 for token throughput. It does not define the meaning of the ± values or identify the significance test. Existing benchmark results retain their previous reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing accuracy, instruction-following and ablation values are unchanged. New results include AraLLaMA versus LLaMA2 subword fertility of 1.7063 versus 5.3844 in v2 Table 1, and word throughput of 20.37 ± 0.04 versus 4.55 ± 0.50 words/second in Table 6. These are added measurements, not improvements over v1 under a previously reported timing protocol.

T1.justification: The vocabulary-expansion formulations and existing definitions are retained. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are added. The new cognitive-mechanisms appendix supplies conceptual motivation rather than mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain progressive vocabulary expansion, AraLLaMA, competitive Arabic performance, preservation of English capabilities and compatibility with LLaMA applications. The introduction retains the threefold decoding-speed claim; the new efficiency experiments supply additional support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting word integrity and fertility to Arabic morphology, memory use and throughput, plus a cognitive explanation of accelerating vocabulary acquisition in Appendix C. Section 3.2 states the previously tentative training-instability argument more categorically. The native-speaker evaluation and deployment limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly documents token embedding initialization, identifies the 2,368 processors as Ascend 910A devices, and reports training durations of 7 and 11 days for the 7B and 13B models. It also supplies language-specific token totals. The abstract adds a model-weight access link where v1 promised a future release.

R1.justification: The new cognitive appendix and tokenizer analysis add literature on vocabulary acquisition and tokenization evaluation, including Krashen 1982, Nakata 2015, Rust et al. 2021, Moosa et al. 2023 and Zouhar et al. 2023. Appendix A's research positioning largely persists; the AceGPT publication update represents the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites and subdivides the methodology, reorganizes existing pretraining material into Section 4.2, and rewrites the benchmark overview. The compression discussion moves into the methodology, and a cognitive-mechanisms appendix changes the appendix organization. These changes extend beyond local copyediting despite the stable core method.

P2.justification: v2 adds tokenizer Table 1 and throughput Table 6, moves the benchmark overview into the appendices as Table 7, and reflows subsequent tables. Figures 1–3 and the existing result-table designs are retained, with limited caption and formatting edits.

improvement.justification: The broader tokenizer comparison and direct timing experiment strengthen v1's primarily compression-based efficiency evidence. Added initialization, hardware, training-time and access information also improve reproducibility. These gains are limited by unspecified timing uncertainty and significance-test details, while stronger training-stability interpretations receive no new controlled evidence. Overall, v2 offers a useful but bounded quality improvement.
